Author a whole instance from one declarative payload — the batch verb.

The doctype-general batch write: applies the equivalent `create` plus N
`add-item` / `set-slot` / `set-field` over a single buffer, persisting once.
In the payload, a slot value is a YAML block scalar wrapped in literal
`<<…>>` markers (`summary: |` then, indented beneath it, `<<the prose>>`) —
required syntax that tags the value as slot prose, not a fill-me
placeholder to delete; the block scalar keeps multi-paragraph and bulleted
prose intact where a quoted flow scalar would fold the line breaks. An
inline field takes a bare value (wrapping one is rejected).

Reach for `author` to write a whole instance in one shot (a migration, or any
many-leaf doc) — it collapses what would be a `create` + N follow-up calls.
Use `create` then `set-slot`/`set-field`/`add-item` for incremental,
one-leaf-at-a-time authoring instead. Run `author` instead of those verbs, or
after them — the create `author` implies over a doc this task already staged
acks `already existed — copied in for update` and changes nothing.

Over a COMMITTED doc `author` copies the committed body in as the edit base
and writes three ways: a payload item the doc does not hold is **appended**
(the committed items stay untouched); an existing doc-level leaf you
re-author overwrites **in place**; and a payload item whose title mints an id
the doc ALREADY holds is refused (`write.already-present`) with the whole
payload rejected and nothing staged — edit that item in place with
`set-slot`/`set-field` instead of re-authoring it here.

The fourth thing it does NOT do is rewrite the doc's title. The payload's
`title:` is the create id-source; over a doc this task already holds (or a
committed one copied in) the `# H1` stays as it is, so a `title:` that would be
silently dropped is refused (`write.title-ignored`) — as is a singleton's, whose
`# H1` is the schema's own `display-title`. A `title:` that mints a DIFFERENT id
is refused too (`write.identity-change`): that is a second document, not a
correction. Both reject the whole payload with nothing staged, and both route at
`jigc doc rename`, the in-task title change.

Payload shape (YAML; `--from-file`), mirroring the document's structure:

```yaml
    title: <the create id-source>
    sections:
      - id: <section-id>
        set:                    # doc-level leaves: fields + slots
          status: accepted      # inline field — a bare value
          summary: |
            <<the slot prose>>   # slot — <<…>>-wrapped block scalar
        items:                  # repeatable rows under this section
          - title: <item id-source>
            set:
              date: 2026-07-11
            sections:           # nested repeatable level, parented by the item
              - id: <nested-section-id>
                set: { note: <<inline slot>> }
      - id: <section-id>        # a section that IS one slot (a simple section):
        set: {<section-id>: <<…>>}   # its own slot, keyed by the section's own id
```

Arguments:
  <DOCTYPE>
          The doctype to author (e.g. `changelog`) — minted through the create-gate

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: `agent` (default, terse text for a coding agent) · `json` (machine-readable) · `human` (formatted for a terminal)
          
          [default: agent]
          [possible values: agent, json, human]

      --from-file <FROM_FILE>
          The payload source: a path, or `-` for stdin (the whole-doc payload is large, so it arrives the same way slot prose does — never inline)

      --task <TASK>
          The active task to scope the write to. Optional: explicit wins; else the single active task; else (zero / more-than-one) the write rejects

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

title: Decisions Log
sections:

    items:
      - title: "Reject a new series over the cap rather than silently evicting an existing one"
        set:
          why: |-
            <<Silently evicting the least-recently-touched series to admit a new one mirrors this codebase's existing overflow precedents (`IngestQueue`, per-series sample trim), but those precedents only ever trim *within* an already-bounded buffer belonging to the same logical entity. Evicting a whole series destroys an unrelated logical entity's entire history, is unrecoverable (nothing else in this repo holds a second copy), and is indistinguishable from an empty/quiet series at read time (`summarize()`'s empty-window branch). An independent robust-case advocate argued this at full strength and it held up when traced through the real call sites. Explicit rejection preserves this milestone's own "age out samples" philosophy (a series ages out its *own* stale data) without extending it to let unrelated churn destroy someone else's data.>>
      - title: "Reclaim only fully-expired buckets to admit a new series at capacity, rather than plain reject-only"
        set:
          why: |-
            <<Plain reject-when-full (no reclaim at all) would let a permanently dormant series monopolize a capacity slot forever once the store reaches `maxSeries`, starving legitimate new series even though the dormant one holds nothing worth keeping. Reclaiming a bucket only when every sample in it is already past the retention cutoff costs no LRU/recency bookkeeping (a plain scan at the one cold path where the store is full and a new series arrives) and destroys nothing the retention contract hasn't already disclaimed.>>
      - title: "Enforce retention inside MemoryStore.put() rather than continuing to rely on Service.tick()"
        set:
          why: |-
            <<Verified that `Service.tick()`'s `prune()` call is never scheduled anywhere (no interval, no loop, no live transport keeps a process alive to run one), and that even if it were, it drains `IngestQueue`, which `Router.ingest()` never feeds — so the existing age-out mechanism is dead on two independent counts relative to real traffic. `Router.ingest()` is the only real write path, so moving retention enforcement onto `MemoryStore.put()`, driven by a caller-supplied `now` (matching the codebase's existing "time is injected, never read from the global" pattern used for `clock.now()`), is what actually makes aging real without adding a store-owned clock or timer.>>

accepted vs series-capped counts instead of silently dropping a
sample with no signal. validate.ts's docstring is corrected: it is no
longer the only place a sample is admitted or rejected.

placeholder until a dedicated config field lands in a later increment
of this milestone.

Store validates clean, and the git history is coherent. Both parts of the task are complete.

**1. Planning** (`a9ff31c`): Verified the baseline by running the actual code — `MemoryStore`'s per-series cap already worked, but distinct-series count was completely unbounded (spiked: 50,000 series held with no eviction), and retention was dead (`Service.tick()`'s `prune()` is never scheduled, and even then drains an `IngestQueue` that `Router.ingest()` never feeds). Ran an independent gap-detection pass and a robust-case advocate to settle the one real design fork — reject a new series over the cap rather than silently evicting an existing one, refined to reclaim only already-expired buckets so a dormant series can't monopolize capacity forever. Recorded all of this in a `planning-record` (every gate answered against verified evidence), a `roadmap` entry with a 3-increment decomposition, a `deferral-ledger` (3 genuinely out-of-scope items), and a `decisions-log`.

**2. Execution** (`35cad37`): Cut the milestone into 3 sub-tasks, implemented each sequentially (they share `store.ts`, so this was a linear spine, not independent parallel work), verified each increment with real tests and spikes along the way, and landed them as one milestone-finalize commit:
- Series-count cap with age-aware admission (reject new series at capacity, or reclaim one that's already fully expired)
- Self-enforced retention on `put()`'s hot path (no dependency on the dead `tick()` path)
- Config wiring (`ROLLUP_MAX_SERIES`) and `store.ts`'s first direct test file

35 tests pass (up from 23), and the store now genuinely bounds both dimensions — verified directly: 50,000 series in with `maxSeries=100` now holds exactly 100.
